lessons.unit: Unit 1: Mastering the sounds
lessons.title: Tajweed audit: what do I know?
objectives: Review the rules taught since Year 1
Use a checklist to rate my own recitation
Set two personal targets

keywords.def: a careful check of what you know and can do

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and basmalah.
Name the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween.
Name the qalqalah letters and the heavy letters.

teach.heading: Our tajweed journey
bullets: Reception to Year 2: letters, vowels, noon and meem rules
teach.note: Pupils recall what they have learned. Ask for one rule each. Celebrate progress: they have covered most of the primary tajweed scheme. Point out that Year 6 is about accuracy and confidence.

teach.heading: The audit sheet
bullets: Makharij: do I know the five areas?
Noon, meem: can I name the rules?
teach.note: Hand out a table with each rule and a 1-3 rating (learning, nearly, secure). Pupils complete it honestly. Reassure: this is for learning, not marks.

teach.heading: Test yourself
bullets: Read the first two lines of Al-Fatihah
Find one rule and name it
teach.note: Pupils record themselves reciting Al-Fatihah and Al-Ikhlas. Replay and tick the checklist. Teach them to listen for the rule names rather than just feeling good or bad.

teach.heading: Targets
teach.note: Pupils choose two targets, e.g. ghunnah length and madd muttasil. Share an example plan: five minutes daily with a recording. Close with a dua for steadfastness.

practice: Name the four rules for noon sakinah.
How many counts is madd lazim?
independent: Complete the audit sheet for all rules
Record and review Al-Fatihah with the checklist
Write two targets with a plan to reach them
exit: Name one rule you are secure on.
lessons.homework: Practise your target daily for five minutes and note how it feels.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audit sheet with icons and examples. Stretch: design a quiz on a rule for classmates.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Mastering the sounds
lessons.title: Similar-sounding letters
objectives: Hear the difference between similar letters
Say them from the right makhraj
Check a recitation for letter mix-ups

keywords.def: the qualities of a letter, e.g. heavy or light
the place a letter comes from

teach.heading: Pairs to master
teach.note: Say each pair with fathah slowly, with your hand at your throat for ح ه ع ء. Heavy ص vs light س; heavy ط vs light ت. Pupils echo and listen to their partner.

teach.heading: More pairs
teach.note: Daad comes from the side of the tongue; Dhaa from the tip between the teeth. Say both slowly. Take care: many learners confuse them. Encourage gentle practice with a teacher.

teach.heading: Check in words
bullets: الْحَمْدُ - the throat letter ح, not ه
teach.note: Use words from Al-Fatihah and Al-Ikhlas. Pupils compare the correct letter and its twin. Ask: what changes if we use the wrong one?

teach.heading: Daily habit
teach.note: Give pupils a way to practise at home: a minute per day on one pair. Remind them: ask a qualified teacher to listen and correct. Teachers cannot be replaced by apps.

practice: Say ص and س. Which is heavy?
Which letter in الْحَمْدُ is from the middle of the throat?
independent: Match 10 word pairs by sound
Read 8 words from the surahs and name the makhraj of each underlined letter
Recite Al-Fatihah and note any pair that needs more work
exit: Which two letters are easy to mix up?
lessons.homework: Choose one pair of similar letters and practise it for one minute a day, then record yourself.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: mouth-position pictures and audio. Stretch: write a tip to help another pupil with one pair.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Inshiqaq and the sifat of strength
lessons.title: Letter qualities: whispered and voiced letters (hams and jahr)
lessons.bigQuestion: Hold a tissue in front of your mouth and say 'at' then 'ad'. Which one moves the tissue?
objectives: To understand the sifat of hams (whispered, breath flows) and jahr (voiced, breath held) and hear them in recitation
successCriteria: All: say the ten hams letters using the phrase
Most: hear the breath on a hams letter with sukoon
Some: explain why a missing breath on ت changes the sound
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: sound, vibration and breath (Year 4 sound)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: care for every detail of Allah's words

keywords.def: the qualities of a letter's sound (singular sifah)
whispered: the breath flows with the letter
voiced: the breath is held back

hook.text: Hold a tissue in front of your mouth and say 'at' then 'ad'. Which one moves the tissue?
hook.a: 'At' (ت) lets a little breath out: hams. 'Ad' (د) holds the breath: jahr.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Knowing each letter's qualities is part of reciting it as it was revealed.

starter.q: Recite Al-Inshiqaq 84:2 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?
Which letters come from the lips?

teach.heading: What are sifat?
bullets: Makhraj: where a letter is made
Two letters, same place, different sifat: ت and د
teach.note: Bismillah. Pupils learned makharij in Year 5. Sifat tell us the quality: whispered or voiced, strong or flowing, raised or lowered.

teach.heading: Hams and jahr
teach.note: The ten hams letters are in the phrase فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتَ. All other letters are jahr.

left.title: Hams (همس): whispered
points: ف ح ث ه ش خ ص س ك ت

teach.heading: Hear it in Al-Inshiqaq
teach.note: A hams letter with sukoon, especially ت and ك, needs a little breath. Model ٱنشَقَّتْ with and without.

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: Without the breath, ت can sound like د.

misconception.wrong: inshaqqad: the final ت closed with no breath
misconception.right: inshaqqat: a light breath after the ت

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: س is in فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتَ. د and ب are jahr.

practice.q: Say «وَحُقَّتْ» (84:2) and show the breath on the ت.
practice.a: wa huq-qat: a light breath after the final ت (hams).
practice.model: I do: I hold a tissue up. وَحُقَّ: the qaf is strong and heavy. تْ: I stop the sound and let a light breath out: the tissue moves.

practice.q: How many hams letters?

independent.q: Tissue test (pupil PDF): say 10 letters with sukoon (اَتْ اَدْ اَسْ ...) and write H or J for each. Today's rota group recites 84:1 to 5 in turn.
independent.a: Hams: ت س ك ف ه ش ح; jahr: د ب ج (from the list on the sheet).
independent.model: The teacher does the first: 'at': the tissue moves, so H.

independent.q: Extend: write the hams phrase from memory.
independent.a: فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتَ

independent.q: Stretch: ت and د are made in the same place. What makes them different?
independent.a: ت is hams (breath flows); د is jahr (breath held).

exit.q: ت with sukoon needs ...
exit.a: a light breath

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Hold a tissue in front of your mouth and say 'at' then 'ad'. Which one moves the tissue?
exit.a: 'At' (ت) lets a little breath out: hams. 'Ad' (د) holds the breath: jahr.

lessons.homework: Do the tissue test with a parent for the ten hams letters, then recite 84:1 to 5; tick the revision log.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

Madinah mushaf (Hafs 'an 'Asim), print or the school's approved mushaf app
Pupil PDF worksheet: Letter qualities rule card and examples
Teacher's own recitation, spoken only (no melody exercises or audio with music)
Portal revision log (pupil ticks daily revision; parent initials)

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Recitation with beauty and care
lessons.title: Tarteel: pace, breath and voice
objectives: Explain tarteel
Recite at a steady pace with good breath control
Show adab in recitation

teach.heading: Allah's command
teach.note: Read the meaning: and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation. Link to tajweed: tarteel is giving each letter its right, calmly. Ask: why would a slower pace help us?

teach.heading: Beautify your voice
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said to beautify the Qur'an with our voices
Reported by Abu Dawud and others
Beauty does not mean showing off
teach.note: The hadith is: زَيِّنُوا الْقُرْآنَ بِأَصْوَاتِكُمْ - beautify the Qur'an with your voices (Abu Dawud, Nasa'i, Ahmad). Explain that the aim is sincere recitation, not performance. Pupils reflect on their intention.

teach.heading: Breath and pace
bullets: Breathe at stops, not in the middle of a word
teach.note: Model a recitation of An-Nas at three speeds: too fast, too slow, steady. Pupils vote which is best and why. Remind them that being steady is a sign of skill.

teach.heading: Adab
bullets: Be in a clean, quiet place
Sit calmly and face the qibla if you can
teach.note: Discuss why adab matters to us. Do not make it a rule list alone; include why each point is respectful. Pupils choose one adab to improve this week.

practice: Which surah has the command to recite with tarteel?
independent: Recite An-Nas at three paces and discuss
Practise breath control with Al-Ikhlas
Reflect: write one way to improve your adab
exit: Why do we avoid showing off in recitation?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Fatihah daily with tarteel and good adab; ask a family member to listen.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pacing gestures and visual breath markers. Stretch: explain the difference between tarteel and hadr.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ash-Sharh and Surat At-Tin
lessons.title: Surat Ash-Sharh: ayat 1-4
objectives: Recite ayat 1-4 accurately
Understand the favours Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ
Find tajweed rules

keywords.def: surah 94: the opening of the chest

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Meaning: Did We not open your chest for you? And We removed your burden. Chunk and echo ayat 1-2. Explain that the surah was a comfort to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-4
teach.note: Meaning: which weighed down your back; and We raised your mention for you. Chunk and echo. Ask: what honour did Allah give the Prophet ﷺ? Every adhan and every salah mention him.

teach.heading: Rules to find
teach.note: Pupils label the rules. Revise the raa: in وِزْرَكَ, ظَهْرَكَ and ذِكْرَكَ the raa carries a fathah, so it is heavy. Ask: what decides if a raa is heavy or light? Its vowel.

teach.heading: Memorise it
teach.note: Memorise ayat 1-2 today and 3-4 at home. Pairs test one another. Praise accuracy of rules as well as memory.

practice: Is the raa in وِزْرَكَ heavy or light?
independent: Read ayat 1-4 in pairs; mark ikhfa and heavy letters
Memorise ayat 1-2, then 3-4
Recite individually
exit: What did Allah raise for the Prophet ﷺ?
lessons.homework: Recite Ash-Sharh ayat 1-4 daily and learn them by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and a translation card. Stretch: learn ayat 1-8.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ash-Sharh and Surat At-Tin
lessons.title: Surat Ash-Sharh: ease after hardship
objectives: Recite ayat 5-8 accurately
Explain the promise of ease
Apply it to a personal situation

teach.heading: Ayat 5-6
teach.note: The promise is repeated for emphasis. Madd 'iwad on يُسْرًا when stopping. Invite pupils to share a time when something difficult became easier.

teach.heading: Ayat 7-8
teach.note: Meaning: when you are free, work hard; and turn to your Lord with desire. Qalqalah on the baa when stopping on فَارْغَب. Ask: how can we use free time well?

teach.heading: Tajweed check
teach.note: Pupils label the rules and practise the echo on the final baa. The noon in فَانصَبْ meets Saad: ikhfa. Both ayat 7 and 8 end with ب.

teach.heading: Living the surah
bullets: Keep trying when things are hard
Make good use of free time
teach.note: Link to exams and homework. Ask pupils for one practical action. Conclude with a short dua for ease. Keep the mood hopeful.

practice: Where is the strong echo in ayat 7-8?
independent: Read ayat 5-8 in pairs; mark madd 'iwad and qalqalah
Memorise ayat 5-8
Recite the whole surah with a partner
exit: What does the repetition of ayat 5 and 6 tell us?
lessons.homework: Recite the whole of Ash-Sharh daily and write one hard thing you will do with hope.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and picture prompts. Stretch: write a dua asking Allah for ease.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ash-Sharh and Surat At-Tin
lessons.title: Surat At-Tin and recital
objectives: Recite At-Tin accurately
Understand its message about human worth and faith
Recite one chosen surah with tajweed
starter: Which rule is in مِن بَعْدِ?

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Allah swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and this safe city. Scholars give different explanations for the fig and olive; no need to choose in class. Chunk and echo ayat 1-3.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-6
bullets: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ
teach.note: Meaning: We created the human in the best form; then returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do good. Link to Al-Asr. Ask: what is the same?

teach.heading: Ayat 7-8
teach.note: Meaning: so what makes you deny the judgement? Is Allah not the best of judges? Chunk and echo. Pupils spot the natural madd in الْحَاكِمِينَ and the heavy laam of Allah in أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ (after a fathah).

teach.heading: Recital
teach.note: Pupils record or recite to the teacher. Provide feedback with one strength and one target. Close with a dua.

practice: How is At-Tin similar to Al-Asr?
independent: Read At-Tin and mark madd and ikhfa
Memorise ayat 1-4
Recite Ash-Sharh or At-Tin with the checklist
exit: What does At-Tin say about how Allah created humans?
Name one tajweed rule in ayah 4.
lessons.homework: Recite At-Tin daily and learn ayat 1-5.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and sentence stems for reflection. Stretch: write a comparison of At-Tin and Al-Asr.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ash-Sharh and Surat At-Tin
lessons.title: How to memorise and keep what we learn
objectives: Use a memorisation routine
Plan daily revision
Recite a surah from memory

keywords.def: older learning that is revised regularly

teach.heading: Allah makes it easy
bullets: Allah has made the Qur'an easy to remember
teach.note: Read the ayah meaning: We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember? Pupils discuss what helps them remember. Encourage them: ease comes from effort and dua.

teach.heading: New and old
teach.note: Draw a three-column plan: sabaq, recent, manzil. Show how a pupil could schedule them over a week. Keep to small, achievable amounts.

teach.heading: Helpful methods
bullets: Test aloud, not in your head
teach.note: Model chaining on Ash-Sharh ayat 5-6, linking the repeated line. Test aloud. Say: mistakes are a sign you are learning. Encourage a regular time of day.

teach.heading: My plan
teach.note: Pupils write a realistic weekly plan. Share a few. Conclude with a dua for a firm memory and sincerity.

practice: Say the ayah about the Qur'an being easy.
independent: Write a weekly revision plan for three surahs
Test a partner on Ash-Sharh
Recite one chosen surah from memory
exit: Name two ways to help memory.
lessons.homework: Follow your plan for a week and record how many days you revised.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: visual planner and audio recordings. Stretch: design a revision poster for younger pupils.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Inshiqaq and the sifat of strength
lessons.title: Surat Al-Inshiqaq 84:1-5: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: What would it look like if the sky split open? Why does the Qur'an describe the Day of Judgement so vividly?
objectives: To memorise Al-Inshiqaq 84:1-5 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 84:1-5 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 84:1-5 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 84:1-5 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the sky and the earth obey Allah; we choose to obey Him too

hook.text: What would it look like if the sky split open? Why does the Qur'an describe the Day of Judgement so vividly?
hook.a: So that we remember it and prepare: the sky and the earth obey their Lord on that Day (84:1 to 5).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'When the sky has split open, and has listened to its Lord and was obligated' (Al-Inshiqaq 84:1 to 2). The whole creation obeys Allah; we choose to obey Him now.

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Inshiqaq 84:1-5
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 84:1-5 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنشَقَّتْ (١) وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ (٢) وَإِذَا ٱلْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ (٣) وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ (٤) وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ (٥)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And has responded to its Lord and was obligated [to do so]
And when the earth has been extended
And has cast out that within it and relinquished [it]
And has responded to its Lord and was obligated [to do so] -

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Light hidden noon; the ت at the end breathes out
Press the daal: mud-dat, breath on the final ت
as-samaa'u: the laam is not said

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 84:1-5 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Teacher recites one ayah (talaqqi)
Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: 84:2: 'and has listened to its Lord and was obligated', meaning it obeyed.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Inshiqaq 84:1-5 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 84:1-5 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 84:1-5. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.q: Which ayah repeats 84:2 word for word?

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 84:1-5 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, write what the earth does in 84:3 to 4.
independent.a: It is spread out, throws out what is in it and becomes empty.

independent.q: 84:2 and 84:5 are the same words. How can a repeated ayah help or trick your memory?
independent.a: It helps (one ayah learned twice) but can trick you into skipping 84:3 to 4; link 84:4 to 84:5 carefully.

exit.q: Al-Inshiqaq 84:3: «وَإِذَا ٱلْأَرْضُ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: مُدَّتْ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: What would it look like if the sky split open? Why does the Qur'an describe the Day of Judgement so vividly?
exit.a: So that we remember it and prepare: the sky and the earth obey their Lord on that Day (84:1 to 5).

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Inshiqaq 84:1-5 to a parent three times a day and revise Surahs 114 to 85 on the rota (today's group); tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Inshiqaq and the sifat of strength
lessons.title: Surat Al-Inshiqaq 84:6-10: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Everyone is working hard towards something. 84:6 says we are all labouring towards our Lord. What does that mean for your day?
objectives: To memorise Al-Inshiqaq 84:6-10 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 84:6-10 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 84:6-10 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 84:6-10 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Moral: our deeds are recorded; we try to fill our book with good

keywords.def: a book; here a person's record of deeds

hook.text: Everyone is working hard towards something. 84:6 says we are all labouring towards our Lord. What does that mean for your day?
hook.a: Every effort leads to meeting Allah; so we make our efforts good. Some will receive their book in the right hand, others behind their backs (84:7 to 10).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O mankind, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with great exertion and will meet it' (Al-Inshiqaq 84:6). Then He describes receiving one's record in the right hand, and an easy account (84:7 to 9).

starter.q: Recite Al-Inshiqaq 84:3 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Inshiqaq 84:6-10
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 84:6-10 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

practice.q: Itbaq letters?

hook.text: When the Qur'an is recited, what should a believer's heart and body do?

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate' (Al-Inshiqaq 84:21). This is one of the places of sajdat at-tilawah (۩): the Prophet ﷺ prostrated when reciting this surah (Bukhari and Muslim).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate [to Allah]?
But those who have disbelieved deny,

teach.note: Point to each word. At ۩ (end of 84:21) explain: this is a place of sajdat at-tilawah; the reciter may prostrate once, saying Allahu Akbar. It is a Sunnah; pupils practise it at home with a parent.

independent.a: All 25 ayat; the pupil points out the sajdah at 84:21.

exit.a: Listen and humble themselves; 84:21 blames those who do not prostrate when the Qur'an is recited. There is a sajdah here.

lessons.title: Itbaq and infitah: covered and open letters
lessons.bigQuestion: Say 'saad' then 'seen', 'taa' (ط) then 'taa' (ت). Where does your tongue go differently?
objectives: To understand how the four covered letters (itbaq) differ from the open letters and why it matters
successCriteria: All: name the four itbaq letters
Most: say each itbaq letter with the tongue covering the roof of the mouth
Some: explain how itbaq keeps ص different from س and ط from ت
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: precision in Allah's words, so each word keeps its meaning

keywords.def: a quality of how a letter is said
the tongue covers the roof of the mouth: ص ض ط ظ
the tongue stays open from the roof of the mouth: all other letters
the back of the tongue rises: a heavy letter

hook.text: Say 'saad' then 'seen', 'taa' (ط) then 'taa' (ت). Where does your tongue go differently?
hook.a: For ص and ط the middle of the tongue rises and covers the roof of the mouth; for س and ت it does not.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Itbaq keeps words apart: صَبْر (patience) and سَبْر are different words.

bullets: The tongue rises and covers the roof

teach.heading: Infitah: the open letters
bullets: Space stays between tongue and roof
teach.note: Compare each itbaq letter with its open partner.

objectives: To memorise Al-Mutaffifin 83:7-12 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 83:7-12 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 83:7-12 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 83:7-12 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Moral: our deeds are recorded; taking responsibility

hook.text: Allah says the record of the wicked is in 'sijjin', 'a register inscribed' (83:7 to 9). Why does it matter that our deeds are written?
hook.a: Nothing is forgotten: good and bad deeds are recorded, so we try to fill our record with good.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in sijjeen.' 'It is [their destination recorded in] a register inscribed.' (Al-Mutaffifin 83:7, 9).

hook.text: Al-Mutaffifin starts with cheating and ends with reward and justice. What is the main lesson for you?
hook.a: Be honest in everything; Allah records it all, and the righteous will be rewarded.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?' (Al-Qamar 54:17).

starter.q: Recite Al-Mutaffifin 83:32 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

check.q: Which letter is both qalqalah and itbaq?
check.why: ط is in قطب جد (qalqalah) and in ص ض ط ظ (itbaq).

practice.q: Recite 83:29 to 36 together.
practice.a: The class recites 83:29 to 36.
practice.model: I do: I recite 83:31 to 32 slowly with each munfasil at four counts and لَضَآلُّونَ at six.

independent.q: Hifdh test: today's group recites Al-Mutaffifin to the teacher. Everyone else completes the qalqalah and itbaq check on the pupil PDF.
independent.a: Rubric marked; written check answers on the teacher sheet.
independent.model: The teacher does question 1 of the written check aloud.

independent.q: Extend: write your target for next half term.
independent.a: For example: 'Keep a short, clean qalqalah with no extra vowel.'

exit.a: Be honest in everything; Allah records it all, and the righteous will be rewarded.

lessons.homework: Revise Al-Mutaffifin and Al-Inshiqaq daily; next half term we learn Al-Infitar.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.
